summary: Per-diem expense lines tagged with incorrect tax-country code causing payroll tax calculation failure
description: Issue summary: Several employee per-diem reimbursements submitted in Feb payroll were denied by the payroll tax validation step. Impact: 18 reimbursements held for UK employees in Feb payrun; tax engine returned mismatch error and blocked release to payroll provider. No funds were sent. Business impact: delayed reimbursements, multiple employee escalations to People Ops.
impact: 18 reimbursements blocked; estimated exposure ~£6.2k; prioritized because this affects employee payroll and People Ops SLAs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Upload expense report with per-diem lines for expense country set to 'United Kingdom' but expense metadata populated with ISO country code 'GBR' in the legacy field.
2) Expense system submits normalized payload to tax-engine endpoint POST /v1/tax/compute with tax_country parameter derived from parser.
3) Tax-engine validation compares tax_country to payroll employee residence and fails with code TAX_COUNTRY_MISMATCH, causing the reimbursement to be flagged and payment withheld.
4) Attempt to re-process using the expense admin console -> same validation error appears in the logs.
expected_result: Per-diem reimbursements should be accepted when employee residence and declared expense country align; tax-engine should accept equivalent ISO representations (GB, GBR, UK) or the expenses pipeline should normalize consistently.
actual_result: Tax-engine rejects lines due to inconsistent tax-country tokenization (GB vs GBR vs UK), returning TAX_COUNTRY_MISMATCH and halting payout.
logs: 2026-03-01T09:12:34Z ERROR tax-engine TAX_COUNTRY_MISMATCH txn=exp_2026_017 id=E-89a3 payload.tax_country=GBR payload.employee_country=GB
2026-03-01T09:12:36Z WARN expenses-parser field-normalization: per_diem.country_code raw='UK' normalized='' txn=exp_2026_017
Payroll provider response: 422 Unprocessable Entity - tax validation failed (reference: PP-INV-20260301-91)
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Finance Ops (Maya): discrepancies appear only for per-diem templates created before the parser normalization patch rolled out on 2026-02-18.

Hypothesis A: legacy expense template stores country codes in a free-text 'country' field (values 'UK', 'United Kingdom') and an older ISO field sometimes contains 'GBR' which the tax-engine does not treat as equivalent to 'GB'.
Hypothesis B: per-diem template omitted explicit 'tax_country' and the expenses-parser attempted to infer from the trip location; inference failed when employee residence differs from trip country.
Reproducible with sample report exp-sample-741: observed mapping table in expenses-parser returned empty for 'UK' and forwarded 'GBR' to tax-engine unchanged.
Related config: normalization mapping file at confluence: https://confluence.redwood/internals/expense-normalization (see historic mapping v1.3 -> v1.6).
Related github PRs: https://github.com/redwood/expenses/pull/842 (parser normalization 2026-02-18), https://github.com/redwood/tax-engine/pull/329 (strict ISO enforcement).
comments: Maya Chen (Finance Ops) 2026-03-01: Noticed spike in 'TAX_COUNTRY_MISMATCH' errors starting 2026-03-01 08:30Z aligned with monthly per-diem submissions. Opening ticket for urgent triage.
Diego Alvarez (Payments) 2026-03-01: Assigned — will validate mapping table and reproduce with a sandbox report. Initial guess: normalization regressions from Feb parser change.

Aisha Patel (Payroll) 2026-03-01: Payroll provider flagged these as high-priority; we should avoid mass reprocessing until fix applied to avoid duplicate payments. Holding payroll run for affected employees.

Diego Alvarez (Payments) 2026-03-02: Reproduced locally with exp-sample-741. Parser returns tax_country='GBR' for template_type='per_diem_old'. Confirmed tax-engine rejects 'GBR'. Preparing patch to normalize 'GBR' -> 'GB'.

Samir Roy (Backend Eng) 2026-03-02: Two possible fixes: (1) quick normalization in expenses service before calling tax-engine; (2) widen tax-engine accepted codes to include legacy values. Recommend quick fix (1) to unblock payroll and follow-up with (2) to prevent future mismatches.
People Ops (via ticket) 2026-03-03: Employees notified that reimbursements will be included in next ad-hoc payrun once cleared. Requesting estimated ETA to resolution.
workaround: Applied temporary normalization rule in expenses service: map legacy values ['UK','United Kingdom','GBR'] -> 'GB' for tax_country prior to tax-engine call. Payroll hold lifted for the 18 affected reimbursements after manual requeue. Change deployed to prod-eu-west at 2026-03-02T17:45Z.
resolution: Workaround deployed and affected reimbursements reprocessed successfully. Root cause: mismatch between legacy free-text country codes from older per-diem templates and stricter ISO validation in tax-engine. Next steps: (1) merge PR to expenses parser to centralize normalization (PR #859) and (2) add integration tests for country-code variants in tax-engine (PR #331). Ownership: Payments -> Diego Alvarez; Tax-engine follow-up -> Samir Roy.
follow_up_tasks: CR-1: Add automated test coverage for country-code variants in tax-engine (owner Samir, target 2026-03-10).
CR-2: Backfill normalization for all legacy per-diem templates and run a one-off reprocess for reimbursements submitted between 2026-01-01 and 2026-02-18 (owner Diego, target 2026-03-12).
CR-3: Update Confluence runbook and notify People Ops of accepted legacy mappings (owner Maya, target 2026-03-05).
